profiles.name: Maria Palmer
profiles.excerpt: Maria Palmer carried an Austrian stage background into American film and radio before becoming a television host and independent producer.
profiles.bio_html:
Maria Palmer was born Maria Pichler in Vienna in 1917 and performed onstage as a child before training in dance, drama and voice. After emigrating to the United States in 1938, she worked in New York theatre and then became a Hollywood film actress during the 1940s.

As film work declined in the 1950s, Palmer expanded into radio, television and commercials. She formed Maria Palmer Enterprises and later hosted the Los Angeles program Sincerely, Maria Palmer, making production and hosting genuine second branches of her career.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves performances credited to Palmer on Escape, Lux Radio Theatre, Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar, A Man Called X, Broadway Is My Beat and Screen Directors Playhouse.

profiles.name: Mike Starr
profiles.excerpt: Mike Starr brought his instantly recognizable New York character-actor voice to a run of modern Twilight Zone Radio Dramas.
profiles.bio_html:
Mike Starr built a long film and television career as a New York character actor, frequently cast as tough men, working-class figures and comic heavies. His distinctive voice made him equally effective in audio drama.

Starr became a recurring performer in The Twilight Zone Radio Dramas, taking leading roles in adaptations including A Most Unusual Camera, The Incredible World of Horace Ford, A Passage for Trumpet and It's a Good Life.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 10 Twilight Zone Radio Dramas performances featuring Starr, documenting a substantial modern audio-drama chapter of his acting career.

profiles.name: Mildred Clinton
profiles.excerpt: Mildred Clinton carried a stage and radio career into CBS Radio Mystery Theater and later film and television character work.
profiles.bio_html:
Mildred Clinton was born in 1914 and developed a career across theatre, radio, film and television. Her professional radio work began decades before the 1970s revival and included dramatic programs during the classic network era.

Clinton later became a recurring performer on CBS Radio Mystery Theater, while screen audiences saw her in films including Serpico and Alice, Sweet Alice and in television roles such as Judge Sussman on The Edge of Night.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves eight CBS Radio Mystery Theater performances credited to Clinton, plus appearances on The Chase and Words at War.

profiles.name: Queenie Leonard
profiles.excerpt: Queenie Leonard brought decades of British stage, cabaret and screen experience to American radio and Hollywood character work.
profiles.bio_html:
Queenie Leonard was born Pearl Walker in England in 1905 and began performing professionally as a teenager. By the time she reached Hollywood in the early 1940s, she already had two decades of stage and screen experience.

Leonard worked as both actress and singer, performing in cabaret, a one-woman show and film before adding television and animation voice work. Her singing therefore remains a genuine second profession alongside acting.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 10 NBC University Theater performances credited to Leonard, documenting her place in postwar American literary radio.

profiles.name: Ray Owens
profiles.excerpt: Ray Owens was a prolific radio and voice actor whose later career included extensive animation work and dozens of CBS Radio Mystery Theater performances.
profiles.bio_html:
Ray Owens was born in 1923 and developed a career centered on voice performance across radio and television. His work eventually extended deeply into animation, where his versatility made him a durable supporting voice.

During the 1970s and early 1980s Owens became one of the busiest repertory performers on CBS Radio Mystery Theater, appearing in a wide range of mystery, historical, supernatural and contemporary stories.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 10 CBS Radio Mystery Theater performances credited to Owens, representing part of a much larger body of work for the series.

profiles.name: Roland Morris
profiles.excerpt: Roland Morris was a West Coast radio repertory actor whose surviving work is strongest in Let George Do It.
profiles.bio_html:
Roland Morris worked in the West Coast radio repertory during the postwar network years. Personal biographical documentation is limited, so his profile remains anchored to the surviving professional record.

Morris appeared repeatedly on Let George Do It and also worked on Father Knows Best, The Halls of Ivy, The Railroad Hour and This Is Your FBI. Those assignments moved him among detective drama, family comedy and anthology programming.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves six Let George Do It performances credited to Morris and one appearance each on four additional series.

profiles.name: Steven Markle
profiles.excerpt: Steven Markle was a later radio-drama repertory actor whose surviving GRH work is concentrated in Sears Radio Theater.
profiles.bio_html:
Steven Markle is best documented in Golden Radio Hour through Sears Radio Theater, the 1979 anthology produced by Elliott Lewis and built around a different dramatic genre for each weekday.

Markle appeared alongside veteran radio performers in mystery, adventure and contemporary stories, including broadcasts such as The Climb, Billy D. Burton, The Visit and The Ransom. The surviving credits establish him as a recurring member of the series' later radio repertory.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 10 Sears Radio Theater performances credited to Markle.

profiles.name: Toby Stephens
profiles.excerpt: Toby Stephens became a major modern radio Philip Marlowe, starring in the BBC’s complete Classic Chandler cycle.
profiles.bio_html:
Toby Stephens built a career across theatre, film, television and radio, bringing classical stage training and a strong dramatic voice to audio work as well as screen roles.

In 2011 the BBC cast Stephens as Philip Marlowe in Classic Chandler, a landmark Radio 4 project adapting all of Raymond Chandler's Marlowe novels. His performance carried the detective through The Big Sleep, Farewell, My Lovely, The Long Goodbye and the rest of the cycle.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves eight BBC Philip Marlowe performances featuring Stephens and two additional BBC science-fiction radio plays.

profiles.name: Torey Carleton
profiles.excerpt: Torey Carleton was a dependable Lux Radio Theatre supporting actress whose surviving work places her inside the program’s early-1940s Hollywood stock company.
profiles.bio_html:
Torey Carleton is best documented through Lux Radio Theatre, where large weekly film adaptations depended on a regular supporting company around the featured stars.

Surviving cast records place Carleton in productions including A Tale of Two Cities, Here Comes Mr. Jordan, Arise, My Love and This Gun for Hire. Her repeated assignments show the practical repertory work required to make those broadcasts function.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 10 Lux Radio Theatre performances credited to Carleton, documenting a concentrated body of professional radio acting.
